clue.text: Invisible force let priest go, somehow

indicators.note: done somehow, in no fixed way, so the letters of the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleric is told to release some unseen power, by whatever means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invisible force' sounds like physics; it is a mischievous spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltergeist is a noisy, unseen spirit said to throw objects about: a force no one can see.

clue.text: Blokes confined by very big threats

indicators.note: the blokes are shut inside the other piece

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing label for very big
blokes are men

explanation.surface: Men surrounded by enormous dangers.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing-size label, a crossword staple for very big.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens are signs warning of what is to come, often bad, so they read as threats.

indicators.note: the first piece lets the second in, holding it inside

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
to err is to blunder or make a mistake

explanation.surface: A dog let into a riverbank after a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a verb, to harass; it is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of dog, and hound is used loosely for any dog.

parts.note: roo is the short, little form of kangaroo, a marsupial
fed means nourished

explanation.surface: A baby kangaroo has been fed and tucked in.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed building has a roof over it, so it is covered overhead.

clue.text: Shocking vote for Republican in charge

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote

explanation.surface: A scandalous ballot backs a Republican to run things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like scandalous; it is literal, giving electric shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something electric carries current and can give a shock.

clue.text: Quiet stroll leading to awkward gait

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an amble is a leisurely stroll

explanation.surface: A silent walk ends in clumsy movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamble is a shuffling, ungainly walk, so it names a clumsy way of moving.

definitions.meaning: a firm is one possible ..., a business or institution
... also means the act of founding or setting up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks a firm as just one example of an establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A business is an establishment, and establishing something is founding it.

indicators.note: reportedly signals words spoken, so these words sound like the answer

parts.note: DI, detective inspector, plus tricked, fooled, gives DI'S TRICKED

explanation.surface: A local area's police inspector has apparently been duped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says DI'S TRICKED is said aloud, sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area of a town or country, a neighbourhood.

clue.text: Steady and true in prudent changes

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it undergo changes, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A careful person who is honest and reliable alters course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges TRUE IN PRUDENT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uninterrupted runs on without a break, so it is constant and continuous.

clue.text: Haggard woman facing Queen is thin

indicators.note: one piece faces the other, so the woman's word stands in front of the Queen's

parts.note: She is the title character of H. Rider Haggard's novel 'She'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A gaunt woman standing before the monarch looks very slender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like an adjective meaning gaunt; it is the novelist H. Rider Haggard, whose She is a famous adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is fine and see-through, so the word describes something very light and delicate.

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other, so the emptied word goes inside the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech, as a sermon is

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving just its outside letters

explanation.surface: A preacher works a hollow parable into a sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like a verb but stands as a noun: the working of a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The working of a machine is its operation; a plant 'in operation' is running.

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor, so ABS are sailors

indicators.note: the shelter stretches across the other piece, so that piece sits inside it

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter
in means current or fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Teetotal seamen pitch a tent on the other side of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a stream to cross; it means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstinent person refrains from alcohol, so is sober by choice.

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman who is not dismissed will ..., read as two words
a short stick, such as a conductor's or a relay runner's

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay indoors and hold firm.
explanation.walkthrough: BAT ON is cricket: a batsman who is not out carries on batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short rod, carried by a conductor, police officer or relay runner.

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first, so the word for about goes last

parts.note: lust is strong passion or desire
re means about or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A warm radiance is about to come after strong desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the soft shine or sheen of a surface.

clue.text: Reason to accept court dispensing goodness

indicators.note: the first piece accepts the second, taking it inside

parts.note: sanity is the power of reason, a sound mind

explanation.surface: A judge's sound judgement lets the court hand out virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispensing' is a link here, meaning yielding or giving out the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is holiness, a state of saintly virtue.

indicators.note: turned over, so the word for provided is read backwards

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'
to reside is to live or stay somewhere

explanation.surface: A householder offers a place to stay the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for home and family life, as in 'fireside comforts'.

parts.note: bras are supports

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the robbery word loses its middle letter

parts.note: a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: The most daring backing for a ruthless raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the I at the centre of HEIST, leaving HEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means impulsive and bold, so the brashest is the most headstrong.

clue.text: Firm holding one new cushy job

indicators.note: one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: secure means firm or stable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A company takes on a new recruit for an easy, well-paid post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company; it means secure, which holds I and N after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position needing little or no work, the easiest of posts.

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so this letter comes first

parts.note: rosier means more hopeful or promising

explanation.surface: A Tory heading a more hopeful workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees; it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosier is the hooked staff carried by a bishop.

clue.text: Government right to give some money

parts.note: the state is the government of a country

explanation.surface: The authorities are entitled to hand out a little cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece, so it is a piece of currency.

clue.text: Iscariot finally with motive for treachery

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the name before it, its last letter

parts.note: a reason is a motive

explanation.surface: Judas Iscariot at last had a reason for his betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or ruler, the gravest form of treachery.

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A crowd is warned that the neighbourhood has gangs now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on of AREA'S GOT GANGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag describes a disorderly rabble, a motley mob of people.

indicators.note: the first piece catches the second, holding it inside

parts.note: a mo, short for moment, is a flash of time, as in 'in a flash'
OTT, over the top, means too much or excessive

explanation.surface: A quick glimpse of something excessive was spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb of seeing; it is a noun, a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb, and a motto is a short guiding saying.

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the walking word goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the ship one is on board
to pace is to walk with steady steps
hip means cool or trendy

explanation.surface: Strolling around a trendy vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the stock signal for going inside SS, steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceship is a vehicle for travel beyond the atmosphere, and craft covers any vessel.

indicators.note: the first piece wears the second, holding it within

parts.note: hats cover the top of the head
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A lover in a hat keeps cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover; it is the heart of 'sweet', E, which goes after the H of HATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat something is to raise its temperature, to make it warm.

indicators.note: words said angrily are thrown about, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble about the meals served at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angrily' rearranges INN MUTTER into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment: whatever feeds and sustains a living thing.

clue.text: Somebody perhaps as redundant extra, initially

definitions.text: Somebody perhaps as redundant extra, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letters of the five words before it are taken

explanation.surface: Someone, at first, may be surplus to requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the five words before 'initially' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare person or part is a surplus extra, held in reserve and not needed now.

clue.text: Lead part, so got in cast

indicators.note: cast suggests something thrown or moulded anew, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor got the starring role in a play's casting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges PART SO GOT IN into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The protagonist is the principal character of a story or play, the one who leads.
